title: Individual differences in uses of humor and their relation to psychological well-being: Development of the Humor Styles Questionnaire

verification.verification_notes: Bibliographic metadata (authors, container, 37(1):48-75, DOI) confirmed via Crossref on 2026-09-24; full text not inspected. The paper develops the Humor Styles Questionnaire distinguishing four humor styles; the aggressive style — sarcastic, ridiculing humor — is classified as potentially maladaptive and is associated with poorer relational outcomes. Recorded also as counterevidence nuance: the same instrument distinguishes adaptive styles (affiliative, self-enhancing), so the documented cost attaches to hostile usage rather than to irony per se, and the study reports personality-level associations rather than effects of a single ironic line. No passage quoted.
